title: Exact Transfer of Bounded Linear Recovery and Relative Weight Hierarchies
description: For an inner code and a target/helper split, shortening and puncturing the inner dual onto the helper coordinates give a canonical nested pair. Its relative generalized Hamming weights are the exact minimum helper-union costs for recovering target subspaces of each dimension. The paper gives an exact finite rank-stratified transfer theorem: minimizing prescribed-coset union-support costs over linear maps into the complete outer functional dual yields the first nonconfined recovery system. After the finite outer-dual-distance gate, this criterion reduces to the corresponding relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance; below either exact threshold, zero-extension preserves every bounded normalized recovery equation and its exact helper support. The one-coordinate specialization recovers the target-constrained weighted coset formula and a Singer-cycle family transfers beyond the ordinary support-distance gate. Consequences include a best-target generalized-weight identity, MDS threshold rigidity, positive-density realization, and bounded service-rate transfer. Separations show that the complete relative-weight hierarchy does not determine bounded repair reliability and that different ambient inner-dual realizations of the same abstract nested pair can have different confinement thresholds. A projective-simplex family gives an explicit non-MDS hierarchy and projective-rank reliability law.
